ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution approximately 65:35 ratio of high-intensity white pixels (lateral lobes) to low-intensity black pixels (central hub and trailing margins).
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant white contiguous regions on the lateral lobes (coordinates extending from mid-fluke to distal tips). Central dark pigmentation forms an irregular 'butterfly' shape anchored at the peduncle attachment, transitioning into heavy mottling and linear streaks across the white fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, narrow V-shaped depression with a calculated interior angle of approximately 45 degrees; the notch apex is sharply defined and located at the vertical centerline.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Extremely jagged and irregular profile; left lobe contains 8-10 distinct high-amplitude peaks (5-15 pixel depth) while the right lobe shows a more fragmented, saw-tooth serration pattern with significant indentations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave upward sweep on the leading edges from the water line to the tips, terminating in distinct, pointed distal corners.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Highly localized circular high-contrast pixel clusters (white/grey) indicating barnacle colonization at the extreme distal tips of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Dense network of multi-directional, low-intensity linear disruptions (rake marks) ranging from 10 to 150 pixels in length, most prevalent on the inner-left and central-right white fields.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Severe irregular tissue loss along the trailing edge of both lobes, characterized by non-symmetrical notches and deep indentations consistent with physical trauma or predation marks.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'X' shaped criss-cross linear abrasion pattern on the lower-left white field near the water line.
